_about: How the review covers each documented WCAG 2.2 failure technique (W3C 'Techniques for WCAG 2.2', failures F1–F114). by: automated = axe rules on every page; measure = measurements on every page; deep = hands-on tests on one page of each layout; judge = the content judge, briefed with the failure and its W3C test procedure; consistency = compared across page types; aaa-not-tested = only for Level AAA criteria this review does not test; obsolete = technology browsers no longer run. checks: rule ids (axe), check ids (signals), judge-<sc>, or collect.<field> for the data the judge reads. A unit test keeps every failure listed and every named check real.

F1.how: The judge compares the reading order of the page text with the screenshot; the Tab trace shows the order in the code.

F2.how: Text that looks like a heading but is not marked up as one is collected for the judge.

F3.how: CSS background images are collected with their size and text, and the judge decides whether they carry information.

F7.how: Applets and plug-in objects no longer run in browsers; any blinking content is found by the motion test.

F8.how: Caption completeness needs the video to be watched: the judge marks it for playback.

F10.how: Tab and Shift+Tab through the page; a loop that Escape, Tab and Shift+Tab cannot leave fails.

F13.how: Charts and instructions that rely on colour are judged from the screenshots and image close-ups.

F14.how: Instructions that refer only to shape or position are judged from the page text.

F15.how: ARIA rules on every page; menus and disclosures are opened and their state is read.

F16.how: Carousels, animations and any part of the first screen still changing after 5 seconds need a pause or stop control.

F20.how: Controls are opened with the keyboard and their state is read again.

F23.how: Media playing sound by itself after load is found and its controls are checked.

F24.how: Text whose colour the site sets with no background colour behind it.

F25.how: A missing title is automated; whether the title says what the page is about is judged.

F26.how: Information given by a symbol alone is judged from the screenshots.

F30.how: Every image is looked at with its alt text: file names, placeholders and names-only fail.

F31.how: The same function is compared across page types.

F32.how: Words spelled with spaces between their letters are collected for the judge.

F33.how: Text laid out in columns with spaces is collected for the judge.

F34.how: Tables made of spaces are collected for the judge.

F36.how: Every field of every form is changed; a form that sends itself fails.

F37.how: Selects, radio buttons and check boxes, in forms and outside them, are changed; a new window or page fails.

F38.how: Images without alt are automated; whether a decorative image is hidden is judged.

F39.how: Decorative images with words in their alt fail.

F40.how: Meta refresh is automated; a page that goes elsewhere by itself while watched fails.

F41.how: Meta refresh is automated; a reload while watched fails.

F42.how: Click handlers on elements the keyboard cannot reach, and reachable ones without a role.

F43.how: List and table markup rules; headings and other structure used for looks are judged.

F44.how: The Tab order is traced; positive tabindex and jumps are checked against the reading order.

F46.how: Tables are collected with their header markup; layout tables with headers fail.

F48.how: A pre block holding a table is collected for the judge.

F49.how: Layout tables are collected; the judge reads them in order.

F50.how: Anything still changing after 5 seconds, drawn by CSS or by script.

F54.how: What hover reveals must also appear with keyboard focus; click handlers must be reachable.

F55.how: Each element is focused; one that drops focus fails.

F58.how: A page that goes elsewhere by itself while watched fails.

F59.how: Elements with click handlers and no role.

F63.how: Link text is judged with its sentence, paragraph and heading.

F65.how: Images, image buttons and image-map areas without alt.

F66.how: Navigation order is compared across page types.

F67.how: Long descriptions are read against the image.

F69.how: Text is doubled; clipping fails when page zoom at 200 % clips it too.

F71.how: Look-alike characters used as text are judged from the page text.

F72.how: ASCII art is judged from the page text and pre blocks.

F73.how: Links in running text marked only by colour.

F74.how: Media alternatives are judged from the page.

F75.how: Videos without captions are judged; their content needs playback.

F78.how: Each keyboard stop is compared with and without focus, pixel by pixel.

F79.how: aria-activedescendant must point at a real element; a stop whose focus is not shown fails 2.4.7.

F80.how: Fields are enlarged with the text and checked for clipping.

F81.how: Required and optional labels are compared; errors must be stated in text.

F82.how: Every part of a split field needs a label.

F83.how: Text over images and gradients is measured against the pixels behind it.

F84.how: AAA profile only: link text alone is judged.

F85.how: After a menu or dialog opens, the next Tab must go into it.

F86.how: Each part of a multi-part field needs its own name.

F89.how: A link whose only content is an image without alt.

F90.how: headers attributes must point at header cells of the same table.

F91.how: Tables are collected with header markup and first-row styling; header rows marked as plain cells fail.

F92.how: role=presentation on tables, lists and headings is collected for the judge.

F93.how: Media that plays by itself needs a way to stop it.

F94.how: Every text size is measured with page zoom and with text-only zoom at 200 %.

F95.how: The pointer is moved onto content shown on hover.

F96.how: Visible words must be part of the accessible name.

F97.how: The page is loaded in portrait and landscape.

F99.how: Single keys are pressed with nothing focused.

F100.how: A 'rotate your device' message is a lock.

F101.how: Controls reacting on press are pressed and released elsewhere.

F102.how: Desktop content must still be on screen or behind a control at 320 px.

F103.how: Form messages must be announced, linked to the field or focused.

F104.how: Text spacing is increased and clipping is measured.

F105.how: Gesture listeners are listed; with none it does not apply, with some the judge checks for a single-tap alternative.

F106.how: Device motion listeners are listed; with none it does not apply.

F107.how: autocomplete values must be valid and match what the field asks.

F108.how: Drag listeners and draggable elements are listed; the judge checks for a click alternative.

F109.how: Pasting into password and code fields is tried.

F110.how: At every keyboard stop, a sticky layer must not hide the focused element.

F111.how: Controls with visible text but no accessible name.

F112.how: Blinking content lasting more than 5 seconds.

F113.how: Audio description needs the video to be watched: the judge marks it for playback.

F114.how: Escape must close hover content without moving the pointer.
